events.title: Rock-ice avalanche, Lirung massif
events.detail: Seismic signal 02:52:10 UTC; USGS classes it as a landslide, M5.2 (ms_vx)

events.title: Rasuwagadhi gauge: last report
events.detail: 1.62 m at 08:40; next report absent by 08:50

events.title: Gyirong Port hit (surveillance camera)
events.detail: Port surveillance video at 10:59 Beijing time (08:44 NPT), after ~22 km and ~3,400 m of descent (Guo et al. 2026); CHWRR gives the same time

events.title: Syabrubesi gauge: last report
events.detail: 3.80 m at 08:50; next report absent by 09:00

events.title: Flood Forecasting Division informed
events.detail: Via Rasuwa District Administration and Betrawati station staff (reported)

events.title: SMS alerts issued (reported time)
events.detail: 679,295 messages reported sent to riverbank areas; receipt not verified

events.title: Betrawati gauge: last report
events.detail: 3.55 m at 09:20 (warning 4.1 m); next report absent by 09:30

events.title: Forecast issued for Galchhi and Mugling
Galchhi gauge starts rising
events.detail: Onset 10:20–10:30; above warning by 10:40; peak 10:50, ~8.8 m above its pre-event level

events.title: Malekhu (Phurke): flood wave arrives
events.detail: Gauge rises 3.35 m → 3.96 m between 11:10 and 11:20, then crosses warning (7.0 m) between 11:20 and 11:30 (7.78 m); CHWRR reports 11:26

events.title: Phurke: above danger level; station and bridge lost (reported)
events.detail: Above danger (8.0 m) between 11:30 and 11:40; last transmitted reading 10.48 m at 11:40, none after (BIPAD). CHWRR reports 11:43

events.title: Second landslide signal at the source
events.detail: 06:00:35 UTC; USGS landslide classification, M4.2 (ms_vx). No second downstream flood is implied

events.title: Reported past Mugling by 13:00
events.detail: Conflicts by a few minutes with the Kali Khola gauge onset (13:10–13:20) ~3 km downstream; the map follows the gauge

events.title: Kali Khola gauge starts rising
events.detail: Onset 13:10–13:20; above warning 14:00; peak 12.35 m at 14:20 (danger level 12.1 m)

events.title: Devghat gauge starts rising
events.detail: Onset 14:30–14:40 in the instrument record. CHWRR reports give 13:20 and 15:20 as arrival

events.title: Devghat peaks at 6.57 m (stage)
events.detail: Below its 7.3 m warning level. Rating-curve estimates (CHWRR): ~5,850 m³/s; ~20 million m³ above baseline

events.title: International Charter activated
events.detail: 14:58 UTC+2 per the Charter record; requested by DHM

story.title: The collapse
story.text: Roughly 100 million m³ of rock and glacier ice (estimates vary by study) breaks off the Lirung massif at ~5,150–5,200 m and drops ~1.2–1.4 km into the valley (estimates vary). Seismometers record the collapse itself.

story.title: A debris flow forms
story.text: The falling mass becomes a debris flow, a fast slurry of mud, rock, ice and water. It scours loose glacial debris and buried ice from the valley floor and, by about 4,000 m, has mixed with river water and sediment as it races down the narrow Lende Khola gorge.

story.title: The border crossing is hit
story.text: The port's surveillance camera shows it reaching the China–Nepal border about seven minutes after the collapse, at Gyirong Port, a busy crossing for traders and pilgrims. At the confluence it surges about 2 km upstream into China.

story.title: Almost no warning downstream
story.text: The flow enters Nepal through Timure and Syabrubesi. This first wave came from the debris flow itself and/or a quick breach of the debris it dumped across the river, not from the barrier lakes, which only began overflowing two days later. Below Syabrubesi it drops its largest boulders and becomes a more water-laden flood. River gauges stop transmitting one after another, so the timing here is bracketed rather than measured.

story.title: Warnings go out
story.text: At 09:15 emergency SMS alerts are dispatched along the river. The flow slows as the valley widens but remains destructive.

story.title: Down the Trishuli
story.text: Below Dhunche the river is the Trishuli. Around Betrawati hydropower projects, bridges and the riverside road are damaged or swept away.

story.title: A long, slower surge
story.text: Lower down the valley is wider and the flood wave travels more slowly, giving authorities time to warn towns further downstream.

story.title: Malekhu
story.text: Around 11:15 the wave reaches Malekhu. Within twenty minutes the river rises past its warning and danger levels; the gauge stops transmitting after 11:40 and the Phurke bridge is lost.

story.title: Past Mugling
story.text: By 13:00 the flood is reported past Mugling. Riverside residents as far as Devghat are told to move away from the banks.

story.title: Reaching the plains
story.text: The rising wave reaches the Devghat gauge between 14:30 and 14:40 in the instrument record (reports give other times). The stage peaks at 6.57 m at 16:00, below the warning level, then falls.

story.title: What the map shows now
story.text: The shaded area is the satellite-mapped extent from the following days, revealed by estimated arrival time. Scrub the timeline or click a key event to revisit any moment.

after.title: Barrier lake warning (China MWR)
after.detail: Border lake ~2 million m³, more inflow expected

after.title: Two new barrier lakes mapped
after.detail: ~12 ha and ~19 ha (UNOSAT 4260, Cartosat-3); CHWRR gives ~16 ha and ~18 ha

after.title: Main barrier lake starts overflowing
after.detail: 17:50 Beijing time (15:35 NPT); outflow ~50 m³/s vs inflow ~23 m³/s (China MWR, via Xu 2026)

after.title: Lake 2 overflows
after.detail: Reported downstream rises; rescues briefly paused

lakes.name: Barrier lake 1
lakes.area: ~12 ha (UNOSAT polygon, 28 Aug); CHWRR ~16 ha; China MWR radar ~10 ha, ~2.2 million m³
lakes.note: Lende–Lirung Khola confluence; likely the main lake surveyed by China's MWR (dam ~60 m high, ~300 m wide; Xu 2026). Overflow from 17:50 Beijing time (15:35 NPT) on 28 Aug. Formed after the event

lakes.name: Barrier lake 2
lakes.note: Below the collapse area; reported overflow 29 Aug. Formed after the event

rows: ~0.72 km² detached ice–rock body (Guo et al., peer reviewed); ~0.76 km² (JMS) or ~0.99 km² (JISRS), at ~5,130–5,200 m; ~2.2 km² (WWA preliminary)
~103 million m³ (JMS); 99 ± 10 million m³ (JISRS); ~110 million m³ (WWA preliminary); ~132 million m³ (ICIMOD preliminary synthesis); up to ~30 million m³ more picked up on the valley floor (WWA)
M5.2 landslide signal (USGS); other agencies' magnitudes differ
14.2 km in ~350 s: a route-average rate (JMS), not a measured flow velocity
~22 km and ~3,400 m of descent to Gyirong Port; flow area ~7.3 km² (Guo et al.); becomes a debris flow by ~4,000 m
source.precursor: ICIMOD reports up to 40 cm of line-of-sight ground deformation at the source in Sentinel-1 radar between 7 Jul and 24 Aug; this is retrospective and does not imply the failure time was predictable. At the Kakani seismic station, Guo et al. find several candidate signals in the ~3 hours before (around 06:04, 06:50 and 08:15–08:19 NPT), some close to eyewitness reports of a snow avalanche and an ice-snow dust cloud. They may be small ice or rock falls, but do not establish a deterministic precursor. Sentinel-2 shows the source glacier's middle and lower parts moving relatively fast through 2024–2026.
source.rain: Satellite rainfall at the source grid cell was low before the failure (4.0 mm in 24 h, 20th percentile; 8.3 mm over 3 days), so heavy rain is not thought to be the main trigger. Local rainfall and initiation remain uncertain. The 7-day mean temperature at the source grid cell (9.43 °C) was above every matching week from 2001–2025 (Li 2026); this describes conditions, not a proven cause. Guo et al. (peer reviewed, ERA5-Land) likewise find limited rain in the final 72 hours and a warmer than average spring and summer (+0.58 °C up to 21 Aug).
source.conflicts: Studies estimate geometry, volume, magnitude and speed differently; each figure is attributed to its source.
